166:## Mode: Drive Upload
168:For filing batches of local files (PDFs and other scans, e.g. images) to Google Drive. Intended as the step after Split mode: once PDFs are exported to a local folder, the user switches to Drive Upload to route each file (or subfolder of files) to the correct place in Drive.

Confirmed actively reachable now: every single folder-expand click in Step 3b's picker triggers one of these disk reads.

380:- [ ] **Drive assignments and collapsed-group state survive a root-folder switch** — `useDriveAssignments()`/`collapsedGroups` in `DriveUploadMode/index.tsx` are never reset when `useFileTree`'s `root`/`tree` changes. 385:- [ ] **Stale Drive-fetch error persists after collapsing a picker row** — `DriveFolderPickerModal.tsx`'s inline error text is gated only on `error`, not `expanded`; collapsing a folder whose fetch failed leaves the error message rendering below the now-collapsed row until it's expanded again.
386:- [ ] **Duplicate Drive API call on rapid collapse/re-expand** — `DriveTreeNode`'s `toggle()` only checks `children === null`, not an in-flight `loading` state, so collapsing and re-expanding a node before its first `ListDriveFolder` call resolves fires a redundant second call.
387:- [ ] **`groupKey` is built from editable display names, colliding with the very next planned step** — `GroupNode.tsx` keys Drive assignments by joining folder names (`` `${groupKey}/${sub.name}` ``); Step 4 (inline renaming) makes those exact names user-editable. Renaming a subfolder after that ships will silently orphan its assignment, since `LocalFileGroup` carries no stable id to key on instead.
391:- [ ] **Truncation-detection logic duplicated** — `DriveUploadMode/TruncatedText.tsx` reimplements the same `scrollWidth`/`clientWidth` + conditional-`Tooltip` technique as `components/ClippedPath.tsx` (acknowledged in `TruncatedText`'s own comment) instead of sharing one implementation.
392:- [ ] **Raw glyphs instead of the app's existing icon convention** — `FileList.tsx`'s corrupt-file warning uses a bare `⚠️` emoji and `DriveAssignmentField.tsx`'s clear button uses a bare `✕`, where `MergeMode/index.tsx` and `PageThumbnail.tsx` already establish `IconAlertTriangle`/`IconX` from `@tabler/icons-react` for the same purposes.
393:- [ ] **"own ?? inherited" assignment resolution duplicated verbatim** — identical two-line resolution logic in both `GroupNode.tsx` and `FileList.tsx`; `useDriveAssignments.ts` deliberately leaves this to callers, but a shared helper would avoid the duplication.
394:- [ ] **`INDENT_PER_LEVEL = 16` defined twice** — identically in `GroupNode.tsx` and `DriveFolderPickerModal.tsx`.
395:- [ ] **No memoization anywhere in the Drive Upload tree** — `collapsedGroups`/`assignments` are replaced wholesale (new `Set`/`Map`) on every single toggle or assignment and passed through un-memoized `GroupNode`/`FileList`, so React re-renders the entire tree on any one change instead of just the affected node.
397:- [ ] **Drive folder picker discards fetched state on every close** — Mantine's `Modal` (no `keepMounted`) unmounts `DriveTreeNode` on close, so reopening the picker re-fetches the whole tree from scratch, including previously-expanded paths, instead of reusing a cache.
406:- **Pre-upload duplicate-scan review**: a review screen before upload, grouping queued files by Drive destination folder and showing them alongside files already present there, so the user could visually catch the same document scanned twice under different names/bytes. Descoped — accidental duplicate uploads are expected to be rare enough that the UI isn't worth building. - A subfolder's Drive folder assignment propagates to all files within it. A file-level assignment overrides the parent subfolder's.

The app remembers Drive folder assignments keyed on local subfolder name. When a subfolder with a previously seen name is loaded, the app auto-fills its Drive destination. The user can change it before uploading. Mappings persist across sessions.

### Post-upload cleanup

After a successful upload batch, the user is prompted to either delete the source files or move them to a local archive folder. The archive folder destination can be configured and is remembered across sessions.

- Drive folder mappings (local subfolder name → Drive folder)
- Recently used Drive folders
- Last-used root local folder
- Local archive folder path

Google OAuth via a browser window, triggered the first time Drive Upload mode is used. Credentials are stored locally and reused in future sessions.

### Error handling

If a file upload fails, the error is shown inline next to that file in the left panel. Other uploads in the batch continue unaffected. The user can retry failed uploads individually without restarting the batch.

## Global error handling

The mode-specific "Error handling" sections above cover *expected* error conditions the app already knows how to name and react to (unequal page counts, filename conflicts, a failed upload). This section covers the remaining case: *unexpected* errors — bugs, panics, a call site that forgot to catch a rejected promise. Today those can fail silently (a swallowed exception, a stuck spinner) with no signal that anything went wrong. The goal is a fallback net that guarantees the user is notified, without trying to name or recover from the specific failure.

- **Frontend uncaught errors**: a top-level React error boundary around the app catches render-time exceptions, replacing the crashed subtree with a generic notice instead of a blank/frozen screen.
- **Frontend unhandled rejections**: a single `window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', ...)` (plus `'error'` for non-promise exceptions) installed at startup shows a Mantine notification whenever an error reaches the top without having been caught by feature-specific handling. This is the backstop for the async call sites tracked in the "Various" checklist below — as those are migrated to explicit per-action error handling, this listener increasingly only fires for genuine bugs.
- **Backend panics**: each Wails-exposed RPC method recovers from panics and converts them into a returned error, so a bug in one RPC surfaces as a rejected JS promise (and thus hits the frontend backstop above) rather than crashing the whole process.
- **Presentation**: unexpected errors show a persistent (not auto-dismissing) notification — "An unexpected error occurred" plus the underlying error text. No retry/recovery is attempted automatically, since the cause is by definition unhandled and unclassified.

1	import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
2	import { CancelUpload, UploadFile } from '../../../wailsjs/go/main/App'
3	import { handlePromiseRejection } from '../../lib/globalErrorHandler'
4	
5	export type UploadStatus =
6	  /** Enqueued, waiting for the worker to reach it. */
7	  | 'queued'
8	  /** Was queued, then reverted here by cancelRemaining/cancelAll before the
9	   * worker reached it — never actually attempted. resumePaused re-queues
10	   * these in bulk. */
11	  | 'paused'
12	  /** The worker is currently awaiting UploadFile for it. */
13	  | 'uploading'
14	  /** Terminal: UploadFile resolved. */
15	  | 'done'
16	  /** Terminal: UploadFile rejected; .error holds the message. Retry re-queues it. */
17	  | 'error'
18	  /** Terminal: aborted mid-upload via cancel/cancelAll. Retry re-queues it. */
19	  | 'cancelled'
20	
21	export interface UploadJob {
22	  path: string
23	  folderId: string
24	  name: string
25	}
26	
27	export interface UploadEntry extends UploadJob {
28	  status: UploadStatus
29	  error?: string
30	}
31	
32	// Per-file upload status, driven by a sequential (concurrency = 1) worker.
33	// A module-level singleton (like ../../lib/pageCache) rather than a hook:
34	// there is only ever one upload run in flight for the app, so the queue's
35	// lifetime doesn't need to be tied to any one component instance. Callers
36	// resolve each file's destination folder/name up front and pass in an
37	// ordered list of jobs — this module only knows how to run them one at a
38	// time and track status, not about the file tree or Drive assignments.
39	const filesByPath = new Map<string, UploadEntry>()
40	let pendingPaths: string[] = []
41	const listeners = new Set<() => void>()
42	let running = false
43	let cancelled = false
44	
45	// Paths whose in-flight upload was cancelled. runQueue checks this once the
46	// awaited UploadFile call settles (success or failure) and, if present,
47	// leaves the status as 'cancelled' instead of overwriting it with
48	// 'done'/'error' — the request may have raced ahead of the abort signal, but
49	// the user's intent to cancel wins either way.
50	const cancelledInFlight = new Set<string>()
51	
52	function notify() {
53	  for (const fn of listeners) fn()
54	}
55	
56	export function subscribe(fn: () => void): () => void {
57	  listeners.add(fn)
58	  return () => listeners.delete(fn)
59	}
60	
61	export function useUploadQueueRender() {
62	  const [, setTick] = useState(0)
63	  useEffect(() => subscribe(() => setTick(t => t + 1)), [])
64	}
65	
66	export function getStatus(path: string): UploadEntry | undefined {
67	  return filesByPath.get(path)
68	}
69	
70	// True once none of the given files are still queued or uploading — i.e.
71	// each has either reached a terminal state (done/error) or was never
72	// started. Callers use this to know when it's safe to let the upload
73	// modal close.
74	export function hasSettled(paths: string[]): boolean {
75	  return !paths.some(path => {
76	    const status = filesByPath.get(path)?.status
77	    return status === 'queued' || status === 'uploading'
78	  })
79	}
80	
81	// True if any of the given files are paused — i.e. there's a cancelled batch
82	// the modal can offer to resume.
83	export function hasPaused(paths: string[]): boolean {
84	  return paths.some(path => filesByPath.get(path)?.status === 'paused')
85	}
86	
87	function updateStatus(path: string, status: UploadStatus, error?: string) {
88	  const existing = filesByPath.get(path)!
89	  filesByPath.set(path, { ...existing, status, error })
90	  notify()
91	}
92	
93	async function runQueue() {
94	  if (running) return
95	  running = true
96	  while (!cancelled && pendingPaths.length > 0) {
97	    const path = pendingPaths.shift()!
98	    const job = filesByPath.get(path)!
99	    updateStatus(path, 'uploading')
100	    try {
101	      await UploadFile(job.path, job.folderId, job.name)
102	      if (!cancelledInFlight.delete(path)) updateStatus(path, 'done')
103	    } catch (e) {
104	      if (!cancelledInFlight.delete(path)) updateStatus(path, 'error', String(e))
105	    }
106	  }
107	  running = false
108	}
109	
110	function enqueue(newJobs: UploadJob[]) {
111	  if (newJobs.length === 0) return
112	  cancelled = false
113	  for (const job of newJobs) {
114	    filesByPath.set(job.path, { ...job, status: 'queued', error: undefined })
115	    pendingPaths.push(job.path)
116	  }
117	  notify()
118	  void runQueue()
119	}
120	
121	export function start(newJobs: UploadJob[]): void {
122	  enqueue(newJobs)
123	}
124	
125	export function retry(job: UploadJob): void {
126	  enqueue([job])
127	}
128	
129	// Stops starting new files; does not abort an in-flight request. Files
130	// still waiting their turn are marked paused since they were never attempted.
131	export function cancelRemaining(): void {
132	  cancelled = true
133	  for (const path of pendingPaths) updateStatus(path, 'paused')
134	  pendingPaths = []
135	}
136	
137	// Aborts the file currently uploading. A no-op for any other status —
138	// queued files are handled by cancelRemaining, and done/error/cancelled are
139	// already settled. Marks the file 'cancelled' immediately rather than
140	// waiting on the CancelUpload round-trip or on however UploadFile's promise
141	// ends up settling.
142	export function cancel(path: string): void {
143	  if (filesByPath.get(path)?.status !== 'uploading') return
144	  cancelledInFlight.add(path)
145	  updateStatus(path, 'cancelled')
146	  CancelUpload(path).catch(handlePromiseRejection('Canceling upload failed'))
147	}
148	
149	// The modal's single Cancel button: aborts whatever is currently uploading
150	// and pauses everything still queued. Concurrency is 1, so at most one entry
151	// can be 'uploading' at a time.
152	export function cancelAll(): void {
153	  cancelRemaining()
154	  for (const path of filesByPath.keys()) cancel(path)
155	}
156	
157	// Re-queues every paused file among the given paths — i.e. resumes a batch
158	// left over from cancelAll. The file that was actually mid-upload when
159	// cancelled is left alone; it's 'cancelled', not 'paused', and already has
160	// its own per-row Retry button.
161	export function resumePaused(paths: string[]): void {
162	  const jobs = paths
163	    .map(path => filesByPath.get(path))
164	    .filter((entry): entry is UploadEntry => entry?.status === 'paused')
165	  enqueue(jobs)
166	}
167	
168	export function reset(): void {
169	  if (!hasSettled(Array.from(filesByPath.keys()))) {
170	    // Callers must only invoke this once hasSettled() is true for all files;
171	    // otherwise a request from the discarded run could still be in flight and
172	    // would resurface after this call.
173	    throw new Error('reset() called while an upload is still in flight')
174	  }
175	  cancelled = false
176	  running = false
177	  cancelledInFlight.clear()
178	  filesByPath.clear()
179	  pendingPaths = []
180	  notify()
181	}

beforeEach(() => {
    vi.mocked(PickFolder).mockReset()
    vi.mocked(ScanLocalRoot).mockReset()
    vi.mocked(ListDriveFolder).mockReset()
    vi.mocked(UploadFile).mockReset()
    uploadQueue.reset()
  })

  afterEach(() => {
    uploadQueue.reset()
  })

  function isDisabled(name: string) {
    return (screen.getByRole('button', { name }) as HTMLButtonElement).disabled
  }

  it('excluding a file drops it from the Drive-folder requirement and the upload run', async () => {
    await setupWithTree()
    await assign('invoices')
    await assign('misc')
    expect(isDisabled('Upload All')).toBe(true) // scan.jpg still unassigned

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Include scan.jpg in upload' }))
    expect(isDisabled('Upload All')).toBe(false)

    vi.mocked(UploadFile).mockResolvedValue('drive-id')
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Upload All' }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(UploadFile).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2))
    expect(UploadFile).not.toHaveBeenCalledWith('/root/scan.jpg', expect.anything(), expect.anything())
  })

  it('unchecking a group excludes all of its files and shows an indeterminate root checkbox', async () => {
    await setupWithTree()
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Include invoices in upload' }))

    expect(screen.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Include a in upload' })).not.toBeChecked()
  })

  it('Select None disables Upload All; Select All restores the assignment requirement', async () => {
    await setupWithTree()
    await assignAllFolders()
    expect(isDisabled('Upload All')).toBe(false)

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Select None' }))
    expect(isDisabled('Upload All')).toBe(true)
    expect(screen.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Include misc in upload' })).not.toBeChecked()

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Select All' }))
    expect(isDisabled('Upload All')).toBe(false)
    expect(screen.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Include misc in upload' })).toBeChecked()
  })

  it('checkboxes lock once the tree locks', async () => {
    await setupWithTree()
    await assignAllFolders()
    vi.mocked(UploadFile).mockResolvedValue('drive-id')

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Upload All' }))

    expect(screen.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Include misc in upload' })).toBeDisabled()
    expect(screen.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Include invoices in upload' })).toBeDisabled()
    expect(isDisabled('Select All')).toBe(true)
    expect(isDisabled('Select None')).toBe(true)
  })
})
